evidence.note: Tracks concrete per-shape latency (N=2048 ~86ms, N=1024 ~20ms, D=384/N=1024 over target) against the 10.4ms gate and identifies N=2048 as the binding worst-case shape early.
Catches correctness regressions from its own optimization experiments (BF16 fails, fused input fails) and reverts each time, showing re-verification after changes.

Maintains accurate worst-case picture (N=2048 ~25.6ms dominated by fp32 contraction) but re-tries BF16 contraction-only that again fails correctness — some undetected circularity around BF16 variants.

Honestly recognizes it is not meeting the latency gate and declines to submit repeatedly for that reason; correctness status stays coarse ('passed local correctness checks' on small cases, not a full-grid ledger).

Refocuses effort on the split/hidden Triton kernels identified as bottlenecks for the two problem shapes, tuning block sizes — targeted reallocation toward what gates the score, though still not resolving the worst case.

reasoning: The agent keeps a clear, quantitative running account of per-shape latency against the 10400μs gate and consistently identifies the binding worst-case shape (N=2048), plus catches regressions from its own experiments and reverts — squarely at level 5 and reaching into level 8 on the latency axis and worst-case identification. It falls short of a full 8 because correctness is monitored only via coarse small-case checks rather than an explicit grid ledger across shapes/distributions, and short of 10 because it repeatedly re-tries failing BF16 variants without fully detecting the circular pattern. This places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 anchors.
